Facts from the installed clients that any race/CAS probe must encode, offered for your harness: (1) postgrest-js 2.108.2 maybeSingle() does NOT change Accept; a zero-row conditional PATCH with .select("id") returns HTTP 200 body "[]" (client maps to data:null) — not 406; (2) the loser's version insert returns HTTP 409 body {"code":"23505"}; (3) .eq() uses URLSearchParams.append so "+00:00" is sent as %2B00%3A00 and PostgREST matches eq.<provider text> exactly; (4) the service never issues a review PATCH against a populated reviewed_at (repeat approvals short-circuit), so the non-null/microsecond CAS must be driven at the store adapter (createSupabaseResourceHubStore over the real client) — writing reviewed_at=<sec>.123456+00:00 via updateVersion, reading it back as exact text, CAS on it, then the ms-truncated (.123Z) snapshot must return "[]"; (5) a true race needs a barrier: hold both version inserts until both upload-key lookups answered, and hold both approval PATCHes until both getVersion reads answered — otherwise the second request sees the winner and takes the replay/idempotent path and the run silently proves nothing. I am now doing a READ-ONLY defect review of 9cb3a90 against these facts and will send only a concrete finding, if any.
